Uses and Administration Potassium canrenoate is a potassium-sparing diuretic with ac- tions and uses similar to those of spironolactone (p.1401). Can- renone (p.1239) is a metabolite common to both drugs, but its contribution to the pharmacological action is unclear. Potassium canrenoate is used in the treatment of refractory oedema associ- ated with heart failure (p.1165) or hepatic disease when an inject- able aldosterone antagonist is required. It may be given in doses of 200 to 400 mg daily, increasing to 800 mg daily in exceptional cases; it is given by slow intravenous injection over a period of 2 to 3 minutes for each 200 mg or by intravenous infusion in glu- cose 5% or sodium chloride 0.9%.
